correctness.rationale: Lagrange interpolation at pairwise distinct boundary values is an invertible linear row map, so each independent energy row supplies a generic degree-(n-1) polynomial. Separate root variables and symmetric invariants establish exactly \((\mathfrak S_{n-1})^m\) over Q and Qbar; no hidden correlation remains in shared boundary variables. Generic polynomial discriminants are irreducible and have one transverse double-root branch; independent row coordinates make the m branch divisors distinct and yield single-factor transposition inertia. The finite algebra is a tensor product of monic polynomial algebras, and a determinant-of-Kronecker-products identity gives trace discriminant product \(\Delta_i^{(n-1)^{m-1}}\). An exact no-dependencies checker verifies interpolation and a concrete \(\mathfrak S_3\times\mathfrak S_3\) specialization, with a degree-nine trace determinant identity; numerical cases are support, not the general proof.

value.rationale: The motivating paper leaves the complete-bipartite generic group as a strict-subgroup-of-full-\((\mathfrak S_{n-1})^m\) question and supplies only one smallest example. The uniform exact direct-product classification determines orbit stabilizers and all joint Galois dependencies for infinitely many nontrivial graph covers. The irreducible branch hypersurfaces, local inertia and trace-discriminant multiplicities give a complete codimension-one geometry and ramification profile usable in specialization and geometric monodromy studies. These are natural sought invariants of this specific family, not an arbitrary finite slice or unsupported numerical gain. Classical invariant theory is used as a tool and is not independently claimed new.
